title: Revalidation marks a fact moved when a sibling heading changes, turns off soft-404 detection after one failed request, and lets a corrupt provider-down record block a host
goal: With no cached previous text, factdiff.window_sections compares the sections the window can enter without reading unrelated sibling headings, so adding, renaming or removing an H2 elsewhere on the page does not fail section_unchanged for a fact whose own text and window are unchanged, while an edit to the fact's own section or the section right after it still fails it; factdiff.madeup_text does not cache a status-0 answer of the made-up sibling as a 404, so a network failure does not turn off soft-404 detection for the host's other sources; and provider.host_down reads a record whose until lies more than DOWN_CAP_S after its at, or after now, as ending at that bound (gate g1: clamp)

gates.question: Does provider.host_down clamp a provider-down record whose until lies beyond DOWN_CAP_S, or ignore it?
options: clamp: read a record whose until lies past at + DOWN_CAP_S, or past now + DOWN_CAP_S, as ending at that bound, so a real recent failure still holds the host for at most the cap
ignore: read such a record as no record, so the host is asked at once
gates.recommendation: clamp: read a record whose until lies past at + DOWN_CAP_S, or past now + DOWN_CAP_S, as ending at that bound, so a real recent failure still holds the host for at most the cap
gates.answer: clamp: read a record whose until lies past at + DOWN_CAP_S, or past now + DOWN_CAP_S, as ending at that bound, so a real recent failure still holds the host for at most the cap
gates.host_unchecked: a design choice in provider.host_down's code (clamp vs ignore a far-future record), not a host setup: 'host' names the documentation host the record is about; check 2 proves the answer on any machine

gates.question: How does window_sections read the sections a window can enter with no previous text without the sibling headings?
options: skip: leave out the section of a following unit under an ancestor of the anchor's heading (a sibling's heading line), keeping the section of the sibling's body
headings: keep the parent's section and compare the sibling heading lines separately
gates.recommendation: skip: leave out the section of a following unit under an ancestor of the anchor's heading (a sibling's heading line), keeping the section of the sibling's body
gates.answer: skip: leave out the section of a following unit under an ancestor of the anchor's heading (a sibling's heading line), keeping the section of the sibling's body

gates.question: How does madeup_text treat an answer with no HTTP status, and how is a str body of that answer read?
options: uncached: return None without caching a status-0 answer (the next source asks again), and provider.doc_text takes a str body as UTF-8
cached-short: cache the status-0 answer for a short time
gates.recommendation: uncached: return None without caching a status-0 answer (the next source asks again), and provider.doc_text takes a str body as UTF-8
gates.answer: uncached: return None without caching a status-0 answer (the next source asks again), and provider.doc_text takes a str body as UTF-8

notes: Verified 2026-10-14 on dee8010364 by a read-only Sonnet verifier (stubs, no network): REAL and a wrong answer (a lookup prints [moved DATE] edited in place for an unchanged fact): window_sections adds the parent's key because a sibling heading unit sits under the parent, and the parent's hash covers every H2 line (repro keys printed 3 sections). Merged here: BG-ugucwe42 (madeup_text, factdiff.py:1044-1051, stores None for any status but 200) and BG-gx4wphry (provider._down_rec, provider.py:529-538, accepts any numeric until). Check 0 also proves the edit-right-after half. Tests: sections asserts of test_pool_rows_are_answered_by_their_tool_... (:1393-1417, 1.8 s) and the revalidate mega-test (madeup about :572-574, down window :610-623); no new id. web-sources.md is mapped to provider.py: read it, edit only if it states the down-record rule. Planning 2026-10-14: the test-selection checks pass before the work by design: they pin behaviour that must stay, and the work extends the named test function with the new assertions (no new test id); the other checks fail on the premise. Planning: check 2 re-pointed to gate g1's answer (clamp): a far-future record written 2 x DOWN_CAP_S ago no longer holds the host, a fresh one still does; it fails now (both hold).
